findings.finding: The draft attributes possible re-execution to replay as well as retries. The source explicitly distinguishes completed activities, which do not re-execute in workflow replay, from unreported outcomes that may retry. Local-store repeatability alone cannot deduplicate a remote effect.

The hosted-only limitation is unsupported by the captured source. Separate Temporal service requirements from whether the service is hosted or self-managed. The proposed Joy behavior is an inference, not validation of Joy.
Activity defaults and workflow-execution defaults are distinguished. Add transient/permanent/unknown-effect classification; do not treat bounded retries as proof of safe effects.

The quoted text changes the source wording and fails literal matching. Use a short exact quote. Persisted timers resume when workers and service become available; this study uses manual input after a host time check, not an automatically firing production timer.

One-file-only is not established as the general transaction boundary by the captured excerpt. State the transaction and journal-mode assumptions; neither local atomicity nor these tests establish atomic remote effects or power-loss durability on this machine.

The RFC permits more than the known-unapplied exception: a client may know the actual request semantics are idempotent. Describe Joy choosing a stricter reconciliation policy as a product decision. Idempotence concerns intended effects, not necessarily identical responses or incidental logging.
